title: Outlook mobile: Purview DLP wait-on-send for iOS and Android
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts and documented controls are supported, and it correctly separates Windows behaviour from unpublished mobile details. Minor corrections should recognise the published baseline DLP licensing and extend two navigation paths beyond their policy-list pages.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Purview DLP wait-on-send support for Outlook for iOS and Android.
claims.quote: Outlook for iOS and Android will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) wait-on-send policies.

claims.claim: The planned feature lets organisations require DLP evaluation before an email is sent.
claims.quote: Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent

claims.claim: Organisations will be able to configure how long users wait for policy evaluation.
claims.quote: configure how long users must wait for policy evaluation to complete.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn says Outlook for Android and iOS does not yet support DLP Wait-to-Send.
claims.quote: Outlook for Android and iOS doesn't yet support *DLP Wait‑to‑Send

claims.claim: Learn does not yet document how the planned mobile wait-on-send experience behaves.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile DLP wait-to-send default rollout release channel timeout override prerequisites. Opened dlp-outlook-mobile-policy-tip-ref and dlp-policy-reference-new-outlook; mobile support remains explicitly unavailable and the detailed wait behaviour is for Windows.

claims.claim: New Outlook for Windows wait-to-send is controlled solely through the two Exchange parameters described.
claims.quote: The wait‑to‑send experience is controlled solely through the following Exchange mailbox parameters:

claims.claim: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled accepts true or false and enables pre-send evaluation when true.
claims.quote: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled*boolean*: true or false.**Default**: false When true, it enables evaluation of the mail for Data loss prevention before mail is sent.

claims.claim: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled defaults to false for the documented Windows experience.
claims.quote: $false: Mail sent from Outlook for Windows to Exchange isn't evaluated by DLP. This value is the default.

claims.claim: The new Outlook Learn page gives a timeout range of 0 to 10,000 seconds.
claims.quote: DLPWaitOnSendTimeout*Integer*: range 0–10,000 seconds.

claims.claim: The Set-OrganizationConfig reference instead permits timeout integers from 0 to 9999.
claims.quote: A valid value is an integer from 0 to 9999.

claims.claim: The documented timeout default is 9999 seconds.
claims.quote: The default value is 9999.

claims.claim: The Windows timeout specifies how long evaluation runs before an override is offered.
claims.quote: The DLPWaitOnSendTimeout parameter specifies how long in seconds Outlook for Windows waits for data loss prevention (DLP) evaluation to complete on a new message before offering an override.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A Windows timeout of 1 to 9998 seconds allows an override after that interval.
claims.quote: A value from 1 to 9998 means Outlook waits for the specified number of seconds before it allows the user to override and send the message without completing DLP evaluation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A Windows timeout of zero exposes Send Anyway immediately.
claims.quote: When DLPWaitOnSendTimeout = 0, user will immediately see “Send Anyway” in the infobar of mail.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A Windows timeout of 9999 prevents sending until evaluation completes.
claims.quote: The value 9999 means the user can't send the message unless the DLP evaluation is complete.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the documented Exchange parameters govern the planned mobile feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android DLP wait on send licensing prerequisites default DLPWaitOnSendEnabled. Opened mobile and new Outlook DLP references and Set-OrganizationConfig; mobile is unsupported and the parameter descriptions name Windows and conditional web applicability, not mobile.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Mobile wait-on-send timeout and Send anyway override behaviour are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile DLP wait-to-send default rollout release channel timeout override prerequisites. Opened mobile DLP reference and new Outlook DLP reference; the former documents ordinary oversharing overrides but no mobile wait-on-send timeout or override experience.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Scope; rationales
claims.claim: The mobile feature's arrival default is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile DLP wait-to-send default rollout release channel timeout override prerequisites. Read roadmap description and mobile DLP reference; neither states the planned feature's default. The disabled Policy Tip UI default concerns a different control.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -DLPWaitOnSendEnabled $true -DLPWaitOnSendTimeout <seconds> configures the documented organisation wait settings.
claims.quote:
[-DLPWaitOnSendEnabled <Boolean>]
    [-DLPWaitOnSendTimeout <Int16>]

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for the two Exchange organisation wait parameters.
claims.quote: Searched: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled DLPWaitOnSendTimeout admin center UI configure. Opened new Outlook DLP reference, Set-OrganizationConfig and oversharing setup; the Group Policy and Cloud Policy routes concern the separate classic Outlook registry setting, not these Exchange parameters.

claims.claim: Running the Exchange command requires assigned permissions that can differ by parameter.
claims.quote: You need to be assigned permissions before you can run this cmdlet. Although this article lists all parameters for the cmdlet, you might not have access to some parameters if they aren't included in the permissions assigned to you.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management is the route to the mobile DLP policy-tip control.
claims.quote: You can access this policy under **Customization** and **Policy Management**.
claims.fix: The path correctly reaches the policy-configuration list but stops early. Extend it to 'Customization > Policy Management > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook > Enabled'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy for the configuration wizard as well as the existing mobile reference for the setting.

claims.claim: Automation for the mobile DLP policy-tip visibility setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook' PowerShell Graph API Cloud Policy. Opened mobile DLP reference and Cloud Policy overview; neither documents an automation call for this setting.

claims.claim: The Apps admin center policy controls policy-tip visibility in Outlook for Android, iOS and macOS.
claims.quote: To enable Policy Tip UI to appear in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS, you must enable the policy listed in the following section in the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center.

claims.claim: The policy is named Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook.
claims.quote: Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook

claims.claim: The mobile policy-tip page says policies can target individuals or groups.
claims.quote: You can target policies to individuals or groups, so you can test and deploy policy tip UI as needed through your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Policy Tip UI is disabled by default in Outlook for Android, iOS and macOS.
claims.quote: Policy Tip UI is turned off by default in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS to allow for administrators to test and perform user training prior to deployment.

claims.claim: The policy-tip visibility setting is not documented as the mobile wait-on-send switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile DLP wait-to-send default rollout release channel timeout override prerequisites. Opened mobile DLP reference and Cloud Policy overview; neither maps the policy-tip visibility setting to mobile wait-on-send.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies leads to the DLP rule and dialog-before-send control.
claims.quote: Sign in to the [Microsoft Purview portal](https://purview.microsoft.com) > **Data loss prevention** > **Policies**
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct policy list but not the rule setting. Extend it to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom (Categories) > Custom (Regulations) > Full directory (Admin units) > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User notifications > On > Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only)'. The cited setup page supplies this route; configure the rule conditions and actions for the intended policy.

claims.claim: The New-DlpComplianceRule call with NotifyUser Owner, NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption Dialog and sensitivity-label conditions configures an oversharing rule.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <DLP Rule Name> -Policy <DLP Policy Name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation

claims.claim: The mobile oversharing dialog is enabled in a DLP rule.
claims.quote: When you enable this feature in a DLP rule, it displays popups for warning, override, or block actions to end users who are sharing labeled or sensitive emails in Outlook for Android and iOS.

claims.claim: Compliance administrator is one of the role groups permitted to create and deploy the documented DLP policies.
claims.quote:
The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of the following role groups

- Compliance administrator

claims.claim: Security administrator is another listed role group for creating and deploying those policies.
claims.quote:
The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of the following role groups

- Compliance administrator
- Compliance data administrator
- Information Protection
- Information Protection Admin
- Security administrator

claims.claim: The documented oversharing policy is scoped to Exchange email and configured through DLP rules in Purview.
claims.quote: To enable these pop-ups, first scope your policy to the Exchange location and then select the **Show policy tip as a dialog for the user before send** option in the policy tip when you create a data loss prevention (DLP) rule for that policy.

claims.quote: In Outlook for Microsoft 365, an oversharing pop-up displays a pop-up before a message is sent.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The mobile reference qualifies oversharing-dialog availability by necessary licences and configuration.
claims.quote: The oversharing dialog is available in DLP for Outlook for Android and iOS users when used with the necessary licenses and configuration.

claims.claim: The mobile reference's Licensing requirements section names no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile iOS Android DLP wait-on-send price meter licensing requirements. Opened dlp-outlook-mobile-policy-tip-ref; its Licensing requirements heading has no content before Policy tips supported in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS.

claims.claim: The Purview service description lists Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 for advanced Outlook for Microsoft 365 policy tips, including oversharing dialogs.
claims.quote:
For advanced DLP policy tip support, which makes additional DLP conditions, advanced classifiers, oversharing dialog, and more available, these licenses are required for each scoped user:

- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5

claims.claim: That advanced policy-tip list includes Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW

claims.claim: That advanced policy-tip list also includes Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection & Governance.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection & Governance

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no licence specific to mobile wait-on-send is published.
claims.quote:
Which licenses provide the rights for a user to benefit from the service?

- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3, Microsoft 365 Business Premium, SharePoint Online Plan 2, OneDrive for Business (Plan 2), Exchange Online Plan 2
claims.fix: Feature-specific licensing remains unpublished, but the standard calls for the known product-level entitlement rather than model unknown. Set licensing.model to 'included' and add: 'Microsoft Purview DLP for Exchange Online requires a qualifying licence, such as Microsoft 365 E3 or E5. Licensing specific to mobile wait-on-send is not yet published.' Retain the separate, qualified advanced desktop policy-tip guidance. The already cited Purview service description supplies the baseline requirement.

claims.claim: No meter specific to mobile wait-on-send is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile iOS Android DLP wait-on-send price meter licensing requirements. Read mobile DLP reference, oversharing setup, and Purview service description DLP licensing section; no mobile wait-on-send meter or price is stated.

claims.claim: The roadmap record names neither a licence nor a meter.
claims.quote: Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent and configure how long users must wait for policy evaluation to complete.

claims.claim: Prerequisites specific to mobile wait-on-send are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile DLP wait-to-send default rollout release channel timeout override prerequisites. Opened mobile DLP reference and oversharing setup; neither states prerequisites for the planned mobile wait-on-send feature.

claims.claim: The desktop oversharing setup page says evaluation duration varies with internet speed, content length and policy count.
claims.quote: The duration for completing the evaluation can vary depending on factors such as internet speed, content length, and the number of policies defined.

claims.claim: No identity or sign-in change is described for mobile wait-on-send.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile DLP wait-on-send identity sign-in authentication. Read roadmap and mobile DLP reference; neither describes an identity or sign-in change. Search results about authentication were general Outlook authentication documentation or unrelated support questions.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes holding a user-initiated send for evaluation, not a new autonomous Outlook action.
claims.quote: Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent and configure how long users must wait for policy evaluation to complete.

claims.claim: Release channels and rollout mechanics for mobile wait-on-send are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile DLP wait-to-send default rollout release channel timeout override prerequisites. Opened mobile DLP reference and read Outlook mobile release-notes excerpt; neither specifies this feature's channels or rollout mechanics beyond the roadmap target.
